content:
设
\[
S_n=\sum_{k=1}^n\frac{1}{n+\sqrt{k}}
=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\frac{1}{1+\frac{\sqrt{k}}{n}}.
\]

当 \(n\to\infty\) 时，\(\frac{\sqrt{k}}{n}\le \frac1{\sqrt n}\to 0\)，因此可用展开式
\[
\frac1{1+t}=1-t+O(t^2).
\]
于是
\[
S_n=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\left(1-\frac{\sqrt{k}}{n}+O\left(\frac{k}{n^2}\right)\right).
\]

化简得
\[
S_n=1-\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^n\sqrt{k}+O\left(\frac1n\right).
\]

因此
\[
1-S_n=\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^n\sqrt{k}+O\left(\frac1n\right).
\]

由黎曼和
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n\sqrt{k}\sim \frac23 n^{3/2},
\]
所以
\[
1-S_n\sim \frac1{n^2}\cdot \frac23 n^{3/2}
=\frac{2}{3\sqrt n}.
\]

故
\[
L=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt n(1-S_n)
=\frac23.
\]

答案：B
